original_question: Given a plurisubharmonic function phi on the unit ball and Demailly's Bergman-type approximants phi_j built from the weighted Bergman spaces H(j phi), determine whether the Monge-Ampere masses at the origin satisfy (dd^c phi_j)^n(0) -> (dd^c phi)^n(0).
target_in_paper: §1.2, Question 8 (Demailly) in the section “The Dirac mass question”
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the local setting of a plurisubharmonic function on the unit ball, the use of Demailly’s Bergman-space approximants built from H(jφ), and the exact issue raised in the paper: whether the Monge–Ampère mass at the origin for the approximants converges to that of φ.
missing_details: The paper assumes the ambient domain is the unit ball B ⊂ ℂ^n.
It explicitly assumes that φ has a well-defined complex Monge–Ampère measure (dd^cφ)^n; the paper notes that one may, for instance, assume φ is locally bounded on B \ {0}.
The weighted Bergman space must be defined precisely as H(jφ) := {f ∈ O(B) : ∫_B |f|^2 e^{-2jφ} dV < +∞}, where dV is Lebesgue measure.
One must choose an orthonormal basis (f_{k,j}) of H(jφ).
The approximants are specifically φ_j := (1/(2j)) log(∑_{k=0}^{+∞} |f_{k,j}|^2).
The quantifier is j → +∞ through positive integers.
The notation “(dd^cφ_j)^n(0)” in the paper refers to the residual Monge–Ampère mass at the origin, i.e. the mass of the measure at {0}, not a pointwise density value.
The paper presents this as a stronger question than the preceding Dirac-mass question; it does not require assuming in advance that (dd^cφ)^n already has a Dirac mass at 0.
refined_question: Let B be the unit ball in ℂ^n, and let φ ∈ PSH(B) be such that its complex Monge–Ampère measure (dd^cφ)^n is well defined (for example, φ may be assumed locally bounded on B \ {0}). For each j ∈ ℕ, define the weighted Bergman space H(jφ) := {f ∈ O(B) : ∫_B |f|^2 e^{-2jφ} dV < +∞}, let (f_{k,j}) be an orthonormal basis of H(jφ), and set φ_j := (1/(2j)) log(∑_{k=0}^{∞} |f_{k,j}|^2). Does one have convergence of the residual Monge–Ampère masses at the origin, namely (dd^cφ_j)^n({0}) → (dd^cφ)^n({0}) as j → ∞?
justification: The draft is aiming at Question 8 (Demailly), not the broader Question 7. In §1.2 the paper first fixes a plurisubharmonic φ on the unit ball B ⊂ ℂ^n with well-defined (dd^cφ)^n, then defines the Bergman spaces H(jφ) and the approximants φ_j exactly as above, and asks whether the Monge–Ampère mass at the origin converges. The sentence immediately after Question 8 explains the role of this formulation: it is stronger than Question 7 because the φ_j have analytic singularities and ν(φ_j,0) → ν(φ,0).
